area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a ranch, a split-level and a condo
area.scope.1.why: Many Des Plaines ranches and split-levels date from the 1950s and 60s, so some run older furnaces and others newer ones.
area.scope.2.why: In a split-level the furnace often sits on the lower level, and the upstairs rooms can run warmer in summer.
area.scope.3.why: In condo buildings, the association's rules on roof access and outdoor units shape when the work is done.
area.scope.4.why: Near the Des Plaines River, basements have flooded before, so a furnace's controls and wiring can need a closer look.
area.scope.5.why: Shops downtown and offices on Golf Road run rooftop units, so roof access and business hours set the work.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your Des Plaines building
area.buildings.1.title: Post-war ranch
area.buildings.1.body: A furnace with central air, in the basement or a utility room. The condenser sits beside the house.
area.buildings.2.title: Split-level
area.buildings.2.body: A furnace on the lower level with central air. Upper rooms can run warmer in summer.
area.buildings.3.title: Condo building
area.buildings.3.body: A furnace or heat pump per unit, with condensers on the roof or a balcony. The association sets the rules.
area.buildings.4.title: Shop or office
area.buildings.4.body: Rooftop units for the stores and offices downtown and along Golf Road.

area.faq.heading: Des Plaines HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Is the furnace in my Des Plaines ranch worth repairing, or does it need replacing?
area.faq.2.q: Do you come out to Des Plaines from Chicago?
area.faq.3.q: Do you work on split-levels and raised ranches?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC work in Des Plaines need a permit?
area.faq.1.a: Often it's worth repairing. We diagnose first, and where the furnace has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.cta.body: Have the make of your furnace or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. In a split-level, tell us which level has the problem.

extras.faq.2.a: Yes. Des Plaines is on our service area list, about 12 miles north-west of the shop at 1225 N Cleaver St, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Yes. Furnace and air conditioning repair and maintenance are on our list of services. Tell us which level isn't heating or cooling, and we start there.
extras.faq.4.a: Replacing a furnace or AC does. The City of Des Plaines has an on-demand permit for a like-for-like swap where the outdoor unit stays put, with one final inspection. A repair or tune-up is a different job. Ask whoever quotes an install who pulls the permit.
